annotations.annotation_text: Page 254 opens Book 2, Chapter 1 ("The Mime of Mick, Nick and the Maggies") during the Age of Heroes phase. This passage continues the children's games and pantomime on the green, Chuff vs. Glugg, the twenty-eight Rainbow Girls, the Angelus bell, featuring Shem (Glugg), Shaun (Chuff), Issy, the Maggies. The nocturnal dream-narrative layers Dublin topography, world mythology, and linguistic alchemy into polysemic prose.
sources: Campbell, Joseph and Robinson, Henry Morton. A Skeleton Key to Finnegans Wake. https://archive.org/details/skeletonkeytofin00camp
McHugh, Roland. Annotations to Finnegans Wake. https://archive.org/details/annotationstofin0000mchu_h5g8
Gordon, John. Finnegans Wake: A Plot Summary. https://johngordonfinnegan.weebly.com
JJDA: Finnegans Wake Genetic Edition. https://jjda.ie

annotations.annotation_text: Book of Kells motif "monks" on page 254 ("The Mime of Mick, Nick and the Maggies"): Joyce equates the Wake's labyrinthine text with the 8th-century illuminated Gospel at Trinity College Dublin within the children's games and pantomime on the green, Chuff vs. Glugg, the twenty-eight Rainbow Girls, the Angelus bell. During this Age of Heroes phase, the monastic scribe and the barnyard Hen both decode divine messages from material surfaces.
sources: Trinity College Dublin: The Book of Kells Online. https://digitalcollections.tcd.ie/concern/works/hm50tr726

annotations.annotation_text: Mid-page polysemic node on page 254 ("The Mime of Mick, Nick and the Maggies"): Joyce weaves multilingual puns across 60+ languages — etymological roots from the Contemporary Literature Press lexicons (Romanian, Scandinavian, Slavic, Classical) intersect with local Dublin speech rhythms. The Age of Heroes dream-logic transforms ordinary syntax into a palimpsest of global literary and mythic references.
sources: Tindall, William York. A Reader's Guide to Finnegans Wake. https://archive.org/details/readersguidetofi00tind
